title: HomeopathyClear
question: How does homeopathy work?
hook: Dilute a remedy 1 in 100, shake it, and repeat thirty times. Count the molecules with Avogadro's number, watch them run out at 12C, find out why 30C would need 10¹⁵ oceans to hold one, then run a fair test against a dummy pill.

explainer.title: A gentler medicine, from 1790
explainer.text: Samuel Hahnemann took cinchona bark while healthy, felt fever-like symptoms, and built homeopathy on it. Around 1800 doctors bled patients and gave mercury purges, so gentle remedies caught on, and homeopathy reached India in the 1830s.

explainer.title: Like cures like, as homeopathy describes it
explainer.text: Homeopathy teaches that a substance that causes symptoms in a healthy person, found in "provings", treats similar symptoms in the sick. A long consultation matches one remedy to the whole person, in the smallest dose.

explainer.title: Dilute and shake until nothing is left
explainer.text: Each C step is 1 part in 100 with hard shaking. A mole holds 6.022 × 10²³ molecules, so by 12C most bottles hold none, and 30C would need about 10¹⁵ Earth oceans to hold one. "Water memory" failed blinded tests.

explainer.title: From plant to sugar pill
explainer.text: A mother tincture is plant material soaked in alcohol. Insoluble things are ground with milk sugar. Drops of the dilution are soaked into sugar globules, and a repertory links symptoms to remedies.

explainer.title: What fair tests show
explainer.text: Many people get better anyway, and people visit healers on their worst days. Randomised, blinded trials compare with a dummy pill. Australia's NHMRC found no condition with reliable evidence it beats placebo; homeopaths and India's CCRH dispute this.

explainer.title: Use it wisely
explainer.text: The pills themselves carry little risk; delaying real treatment does. Never stop prescribed medicine, see a qualified doctor for serious illness, and keep vaccines up to date. Many choose homeopathy to feel heard: an Indian GP visit averages about 2 minutes.

concepts.def: A system of medicine founded by Samuel Hahnemann around 1796, built on "like cures like" and highly diluted remedies.
"Let like be cured by like": homeopathy's principle that what causes symptoms in the healthy treats them in the sick.
A test in which healthy volunteers take a substance and record their symptoms.
Repeated dilution with vigorous shaking (succussion). 30C means 1 part in 10⁶⁰.
6.022 × 10²³, the number of particles in one mole of a substance.
The starting liquid for a plant remedy: plant material soaked in alcohol and filtered.
An index of symptoms, each listing the remedies linked to it.
A dummy treatment. Fair tests compare a remedy with one to see if it adds anything.
After an unusually bad day, the next ones tend to be closer to normal, with or without treatment.
